title: Atoms, elements and compounds
intro: Everything is made of tiny atoms. Learn the difference between elements, compounds and mixtures, chemical symbols and simple formulae.
description: Free KS3 Chemistry questions with answers on atoms, elements, compounds and mixtures: chemical symbols, the periodic table and simple formulae like H₂O and CO₂. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9.

questions.q: What is an **atom**?
options: The smallest part of an element that can exist
questions.hint: Think about the tiniest building block of every substance.
questions.explain: An atom is the smallest particle of an element. Everything around you is made of atoms.

questions.q: What is an **element**?
options: A substance made of only one type of atom
A substance made of two types of atom joined together
questions.hint: “Element” means the simplest kind of substance.
questions.explain: An element contains only one type of atom. Oxygen, iron and gold are elements.

questions.q: Which of these is an element?
questions.hint: Which one can't be split into simpler substances?
questions.explain: Iron is an element: it is made only of iron atoms. Water and salt are compounds, and air is a mixture.

questions.q: Where are all the elements listed?
questions.hint: It's a big chart on the wall of every science lab.
questions.explain: All the elements are arranged in the periodic table. Metals are on the left and in the middle; non-metals are on the right.

questions.q: About how many elements are known today?
questions.hint: It's more than 100, but not many more.
questions.explain: Scientists know about 118 elements. Fewer than 100 of them are found in nature; the rest have been made in laboratories.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for **oxygen**?
questions.hint: Most symbols use the first letter of the name.
questions.explain: Oxygen's symbol is O.

questions.q: Which element has the symbol **C**?
questions.hint: It's in diamonds, pencil lead and every living thing.
questions.explain: C is carbon. Calcium is Ca, chlorine is Cl and copper is Cu.

questions.q: Which symbol is written correctly?
questions.hint: Symbols start with a capital letter. If there's a second letter, it's small.
questions.explain: Na (sodium) is correct: a capital first letter and a small second letter.

questions.q: The symbol **Fe** stands for which element?
questions.hint: Some symbols come from Latin names. Iron in Latin is “ferrum”.
questions.explain: Fe is iron, from the Latin word ferrum. Lead is Pb, from the Latin plumbum.

questions.q: Which pair is correct?
questions.hint: Gold comes from Latin “aurum”. Potassium comes from “kalium”.
questions.explain: Au is gold and K is potassium. Silver is Ag, krypton is Kr and P is phosphorus.

questions.q: What is a **compound**?
options: Two or more elements chemically joined together
One type of atom on its own
A pure element that is a metal
questions.hint: Com- means “together”.
questions.explain: A compound has two or more different elements chemically joined. Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.

questions.q: Water is H₂O. How many **hydrogen** atoms are in one molecule of water?
questions.hint: The small number after H tells you how many H atoms.
questions.explain: H₂ means 2 hydrogen atoms. There is 1 oxygen atom (no number means 1).

questions.q: How many atoms **altogether** are in one molecule of carbon dioxide, CO₂?
questions.hint: 1 carbon atom + how many oxygen atoms?
questions.explain: CO₂ has 1 carbon atom and 2 oxygen atoms: 3 atoms altogether.

questions.q: Sodium chloride (table salt) is made from which elements?
questions.hint: The name of the compound tells you.
questions.explain: Sodium chloride is made of sodium and chlorine. A name ending in -ide usually means the compound has two elements.

questions.q: Methane is CH₄. How many atoms are in one molecule?
questions.hint: Count the carbon atoms, then the hydrogen atoms.
questions.explain: 1 carbon + 4 hydrogen = 5 atoms.

questions.q: Sodium is a soft metal that reacts with water. Chlorine is a poisonous gas. What is sodium chloride like?
options: A safe white solid we put on food
A mixture of a metal and a gas
questions.hint: A compound has new properties, different from its elements.
questions.explain: When elements join to make a compound, it has completely new properties. Sodium chloride is table salt.

questions.q: Air is made of nitrogen, oxygen and other gases that are not joined together. What is air?
questions.hint: Are the gases chemically joined?
questions.explain: The gases in air are mixed, not joined, so air is a mixture.

questions.q: Which of these is a compound?
questions.hint: Look for two different elements joined together.
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide is carbon and oxygen joined. Oxygen and gold are elements; sea water is a mixture.

questions.q: Oxygen gas is O₂: two oxygen atoms joined. Is O₂ an element or a compound?
questions.hint: How many different types of atom are there?
questions.explain: O₂ is an element, because it only has one type of atom. It's a molecule, but not a compound.

questions.q: Iron filings and sulfur powder are stirred together. Which is true?
options: It's a mixture: a magnet can pull out the iron
It's a compound called iron sulfide
The iron and sulfur are chemically joined
questions.hint: Has a chemical reaction happened just by stirring?
questions.explain: Stirring only mixes them, so you can still separate the iron with a magnet. Heating them makes them react to form the compound iron sulfide, which isn't magnetic like iron.
